# Ariadne

> Ariadne is a local-first multilingual memory server for Codex, Claude Code, and any MCP client.

## Core facts

- Project site: https://mclaut.github.io/ariadne/
- Hugging Face Space: https://huggingface.co/spaces/mclaut/ariadne
- Source and documentation: https://github.com/mclaut/ariadne
- Latest release: https://github.com/mclaut/ariadne/releases/latest
- License: MIT
- Platforms: Windows x64, macOS Intel and Apple Silicon, Linux x64 and ARM64
- Runtime: Go MCP server, Qdrant vector server, Ollama bge-m3 embeddings
- Retrieval: exact lookup by ID or hybrid dense plus BM25 sparse search, with wing, room, and collection scopes plus bounded historical-intent reranking
- MCP tools: memory_save, memory_recall, memory_delete, memory_move, credential_access
- Privacy: local endpoints by default; Qdrant binds to 127.0.0.1; project scope is default-deny; cross-wing recall requires a visible human approval
- Lifecycle: scoped append-only identities retain superseded and orphaned history for exact-ID audit
- Maintenance: incremental memfile sync, JSON-only guarded diary consolidation, bounded retries, a 20-minute child deadline, and append-only health activity
- Token efficiency: measured savings, estimated legacy attribution, unattributed recall delivery, and signed net are reported separately without storing content

## Install

Windows uses install.ps1. Linux and macOS use install.sh. Both are available in the repository root.

## Current release

v0.8.15 adds a signed macOS `Ariadne.app` with a native icon to Applications. Launching it from Finder, Spotlight, or Launchpad starts the managed tray LaunchAgent and re-registers its canonical plist when needed without creating an unmanaged duplicate.

v0.8.12 adds owner-approved persistent credential trust for one exact source wing, target wing, resource, and purpose; every use, trust, and revocation remains append-only. It also explicitly disables Ollama thinking for schema-bound consolidation JSON and gives the maintenance supervisor a 20-minute default deadline, so an unresponsive child cannot leave scheduled maintenance stuck for hours. v0.8.11 guarantees one desktop tray through a Unix file lock or Windows named mutex, reconciles canonical and historical macOS launchd jobs on every install, archives superseded plist files without deletion, and teaches doctor to count actual tray processes. v0.8.10 makes attribution auditable: Qdrant pagination preserves unsigned 64-bit offsets exactly, corpus coverage separates recallable memory from inactive or security-excluded history, measured source provenance remains distinct from conservative legacy estimates, remaining diary/consolidation/manual gaps are explicit, and attribution backfill is read-only until `--apply`. v0.8.9 prevents Qdrant file-descriptor exhaustion under many concurrent MCP sessions: each process uses one gRPC connection, macOS launchd grants 8192 descriptors, startup creates only missing payload indexes, clients close cleanly, and status/tray/doctor report descriptor pressure. v0.8.8 adds fail-closed remote Qdrant API-key/TLS policy, append-only metrics v3 daily rollups and indexed recent reads, complete paginated collection reconciliation, deterministic judged BM25-versus-learned-sparse evaluation, reusable maintenance retries, and reversible site cleanup. v0.8.7 verified Start, Stop, and Restart by observing Qdrant and Ollama state and PIDs, requiring a green collection before success, resolving Homebrew under launchd's restricted PATH, attempting recovery after partial stop failures, and delivering completion from the replacement tray through an append-only notification journal. v0.8.6 added deliberate Approve/Deny prompts and persistent Claude recall across context transitions. v0.8.3 introduced scoped cross-wing and separate one-shot credential grants, while v0.8.2 made project scope default-deny and added secret blocking plus append-only quarantine. The approval handshake is audited agent policy, not an operating-system credential broker.
